distractors.reason: 'Much' is used with verbs (I like it very much) or uncountable nouns, not directly before an adjective like 'happy'.
'Big' describes size, so 'big happy' is not a natural English phrase.
'Many' goes with countable nouns (many friends), not with adjectives such as 'happy'.

example_sentence: I feel ___ happy on my birthday.
l1_interference: Українці можуть подумати, що 'дуже' в англійській завжди перекладається як 'much' або 'big', тому кажуть 'much happy' або 'big happy'. Перед прикметником у англійській ставимо 'very', а 'much' використовуємо з дієсловами, наприклад 'I like it very much'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the usual degree adverb before an adjective like 'happy'. It makes the adjective stronger without changing its basic meaning.

related_collocations.example: The birthday cake was very tasty.
Thank you, that is a really nice present.
The clown on my birthday was so funny.

memory_tip: VERY goes before adjectives (very happy, very tasty) | MUCH goes after verbs (I like it very much)
